subject: Topology-specific operator access & temporary audit window (MSA / Order Form addendum)
messages:
From: Julia Hart <julia.hart@medisys-health.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-16T08:12:00Z
Subject: MSA/Order Form: topology-specific operator access & audit window

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the demo last week. As we start to draft the Order Form and MSA addendum for the on-prem deployment, legal and procurement asked us to get clarity on three items so they can proceed with a redline pass:

1) Operator access boundary: which Redwood personnel (by role) will be able to access the on-prem runtime image and logs during normal operations vs. during a support engagement? We need a short list and a sample attestation statement.

2) Temporary audit window: for our SOC/third-party audit later this year, we may require a one-time temporary console access window for our auditors and/or a Redwood operator-attested snapshot transfer. Can you confirm how long a window you can support (days), any constraints, and whether this requires an MSA exhibit?

3) Evidence deliverables: what artifacts can Redwood provide (runbooks, logs, witness statements, snapshot manifest) to satisfy procurement and our external auditor?

I attached a quick Excel with our initial schedule and the procurement contact. Procurement/Legal (cc'd) will expect concrete language for the MSA addendum and a proposed timeline for the audit window.

Appreciate a short summary we can share with legal.

Thanks,
Julia Hart
Director, IT Procurement
MediSys Health
Attachment: MediSys_Initial_Requirements.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Julia Hart <julia.hart@medisys-health.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-16T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: MSA/Order Form: topology-specific operator access & audit window

Julia —

Thanks for laying this out and for the spreadsheet. Quick summary below so you have something to share with procurement and legal:

Operator access boundary (high level):
- Day-to-day: no Redwood personnel have interactive access to customer-hosted containers/VMs. Support is via curated artifacts and authenticated remote session orchestration (customer-initiated).
- Support engagements: roles that may be granted temporary access (with customer approval & logging): Support Engineer, Field SRE, and Security Engineer. Access is time-limited, logged, and requires a documented runbook + customer approval ticket.
- Attestation: we can provide an operator attestation letter signed by our Head of Security that lists the roles and the procedures used for granting access.

Temporary audit window:
- We can support a one-time temporary audit window of up to 5 business days for live console access, or alternatively provide a witnessed snapshot transfer and sealed manifest if live access is not acceptable.
- Constraints: 72-hour notice preferred, we require a joint scope call to agree read-only binding scopes and a mutually-agreed runbook. Windows longer than 5 business days need pre-approved SLA amendments.

Evidence deliverables:
- Runbook excerpt (operator access workflow), access logs (time-limited extracts), signed attestation letter, snapshot manifest with checksums, and a brief witness statement from the operator who performed the snapshot.

I've attached a short draft of the operator-boundary language we typically share — this should help legal form the MSA exhibit. For the audit window, if you prefer a witnessed snapshot we can draft the witness script and a transfer checklist.

Next steps:
1) Can procurement confirm whether they prefer a live window vs. witnessed snapshot?
2) If live window, confirm preferred dates (we'll schedule a scope call).
3) I'll ask legal (Lauren) to send targeted redline language for the MSA addendum.

Ben
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_privdeploy_operator_boundary_draft.pdf

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-16T14:22:00Z
Subject: RE: MSA/Order Form: topology-specific operator access & audit window

Ben / team —

Thanks Ben; forwarding to formalize legal's position for the addendum. High-level redline asks / changes we should propose to MediSys legal:

1) Clear role definitions in exhibit: define "Support Engineer", "Field SRE", and "Security Engineer" with permissible actions (read-only vs. interactive maintenance). Avoid open-ended "operator" language.

2) Timeboxed access: any live access must be approved via customer ticket and limited to the agreed window (document in Order Form Exhibit). Redwood will retain all access logs and provide them as part of the evidence bundle.

3) Audit window mechanics: propose two options in the exhibit — (A) one-time live access window (up to 5 business days) under strict read-only / monitored session; (B) witnessed snapshot transfer + sealed manifest. Include acceptance criteria for the snapshot (hashing algorithm, checksum delivery, witness sign-off).

4) Liability carveouts and data handling: limited scope for forensic access; no broader production rights. Add a clause that any remediation requiring code or binary transfer requires specific exhibits and indemnity carveouts to be negotiated separately.

5) Proof of operator competence: we can provide a standard operator attestation template but request MediSys accept a standard template instead of bespoke statements for each event.

I attached a starter MSA addendum with the suggested exhibit language — please review and call out anything product would not be able to support in practice. David, Marissa: can you validate operational feasibility on the snapshot manifest and runbook items?

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
Attachment: MSA_Addendum_Draft_redlines.docx

From: Julia Hart <julia.hart@medisys-health.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement <procurement@medisys-health.com>, legal <legal@medisys-health.com>
Date: 2028-05-17T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: MSA/Order Form: topology-specific operator access & audit window

Ben / Lauren —

Appreciate the clarity and the draft language. Procurement and legal reviewed the options and prefer the witnessed snapshot transfer route (option B) for our initial engagement; we will reserve the right to request a live window for a specific future audit but prefer the lower-risk snapshot approach now.

A few confirmations we need before routing redlines:
- Snapshot acceptance criteria: please confirm hashing algorithm (we prefer SHA-256), manifest format (JSON or CSV), and whether you can provide automated checksum verification during transfer.
- Witnessing: MediSys will require a Redwood operator witness to perform the snapshot with a short recorded witness statement. Can you confirm the operator role and that the witness statement will be signed and time-stamped?
- Timeline: procurement would like the exhibit language to show a 10-business-day turnaround from signature to snapshot transfer readiness. Is that workable?

Procurement follow-up: procurement@medisys-health.com will send the official redline set once we receive the MSA addendum document and the snapshot acceptance checklist.

If all good, we can proceed to redline and loop DocuSign once both sides have the exhibit nailed down.

Thanks —
Julia Hart
Director, IT Procurement
MediSys Health
Attachment: MediSys_Audit_Scope.pdf
